title: Reasons Of Muslim League Pact With Congress
definition: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was a landmark agreement between the Indian National Congress (INC) and the All-India Muslim League (AIML) to present a united front to the British government, characterized by the Congress's acceptance of separate electorates for Muslims.
importanceInUpsc: This topic is central to understanding the evolution of communal politics, the shift in Congress policy towards minority representation, and the temporary phase of Hindu-Muslim unity during the Home Rule Movement era.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Reasons Of Muslim League Pact With Congress.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
